environment: LINUX-CPU (Ubuntu, Node 20, pnpm; deterministic parsing contract only — no speech engine, no real user speech)
scope: Voice technique-intent robustness expansion (extends d4-10 voice-intent-v1): misspellings/ASR variants, fillers, multi-intent phrases, non-technique speech (idioms reusing technique words), ambiguous terms. Unknowns re-prompt, never silently mis-select.

implemented.module: packages/shared-types/src/voiceTechniqueIntent.ts — voice-intent-v1 → voice-intent-v2 (versioned, not softened in place; v2 strictly reduces silent accepts, never adds them)
changes: bounded misspelling/ASR-variant lexicon added to the component grammar (forhand/fourhand/four hand, backand/bakhand, volly/vollie/voley, serv/surve, crosscort, ernie, half-volly, plural sides)

bounded NON_TECHNIQUE_IDIOMS scrub list (serve dinner / serves you right / return my call / return it / drop me off / drop it / kitchen counter / countertop / on a roll / let's roll / roll out / block out|of / roadblock / drive home|to|back…): idiom spans are removed before technique detection so everyday speech resolves to honest unknown + re-prompt
multi-side detection (detectSides): 'forehand and backhand dink' now stays a coarse both-sides candidate set (v1 silently guessed forehand); two-hand phrases still count as one side

spoken-family filter: when the only family-bearing word IS a stroke family name (volley/dink/serve/return), candidates stay within that family so compound slugs (volley serve → SERVE, volley reset → RESET) no longer leak into the option set — 'forehand volley' now resolves FOREHAND_VOLLEY instead of a spurious 3-way ambiguity
fillers required no code change (bounded keyword grammar ignores them) — verified by the filler category below
tests: packages/shared-types/test/voiceUtteranceEvalCorpus.ts (73-utterance labeled synthetic corpus, 8 categories, projection-level golds)
packages/shared-types/test/voiceUtteranceEval.test.ts (metrics harness: accuracy + false-accept rate; hard invariants: 0 false accepts, ≥95% accuracy, multi-intent/non-technique never resolve)
apps/mobile/__tests__/voiceIntentCorpus.test.ts extended with misspelling-leaf, multi-intent, and idiom sections (61 → 78 tests)

metrics.corpus: 73 synthetic utterances: clean 12, misspelling 13, filler 8, multi_intent 8, non_technique 14 (incl. 12 idiom traps), ambiguous_term 7, auto 6, unselectable_specialty 5
metrics.false_accept_definition: projection returns status 'resolved' (the only silent-select path in TechniqueIntentPicker) when gold is not resolved, or resolved to the wrong canonical

baseline_voice_intent_v1.false_accepts: 6/73 = 8.2% overall (multi_intent 2/8 = 25%: 'forehand and backhand dink'→FOREHAND_DINK, 'forehand or backhand drive'→FOREHAND_DRIVE; non_technique 4/14 = 28.6%: 'serve dinner tonight'→SERVE, 'that serves you right'→SERVE, 'return my call later'→RETURN, 'can you return it'→RETURN)
baseline_voice_intent_v1.other_misses: misspellings 4/13 correct (31%); 'forehand volley' ambiguous instead of FOREHAND_VOLLEY (compound-slug leak)

after_voice_intent_v2.resolution_accuracy: 73/73 = 100% (per category: clean 12/12, misspelling 13/13, filler 8/8, multi_intent 8/8, non_technique 14/14, ambiguous_term 7/7, auto 6/6, unselectable_specialty 5/5)

metrics.honesty_note: Corpus is synthetic and hand-written; 100% reflects a deterministic grammar evaluated on a corpus authored with achievable projection-level golds (golds for inherently coarse phrases are 'ambiguous', not resolved). No real speech, no Mac/iPhone dictation measurements (BLOCKED_EXTERNAL for real-ASR error rates). Baseline numbers were measured by running the identical harness at the pre-change commit state.
